❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: Inadequate case coverage

* Insufficient coverage of non-periodic inputs: Most cases use highly regular or periodic inputs. Among the non-periodic cases with output ≠ -1, only Validator 2 contains characters whose frequencies are odd.

In all the non-periodic cases with output = -1, every character in the input string occurs exactly once. There are no cases with a mix of various frequencies.

* Insufficient coverage of impossible strings with mixed character frequencies: In all cases where the output is -1, either every character occurs an odd number of times or every character occurs an even number of times. There are no cases where the output is -1 with a mix of odd and even frequencies.

- I assume you have to select indices [[i]] and [[j]] such that [[i]] ≠ [[j]]. Otherwise, it will always be possible to make [[s]] an empty string.

- The current problem might be too difficult for a clash given the complexity required of the solution. Consider making it a puzzle instead :)

Goal
* Consider stating the character range as ASCII values 32 through 126, inclusive (instead of "from ' ' and '~'"), for clarity.

* Please swap the second and third bullet points so that the removal operation is described before its cost. (The cost definition currently separates the two parts of a single operation.)

* Consider highlighting "exclusive" and "inclusive" in <<bold>>.

Constraints
* Please replace "|s|" with "length of [[s]]" and remove the explanation of the notation.

* The second constraint could be removed to avoid repetition.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer.

Cases
* Currently, every test and its validator seem to cover the same scenario, which is good. However, please adjust input lengths of the following cases for greater consistency:

  • Validators 2, 3 and 4: around 20.

  • Test 6 and Validator 6: around 50.

  • Test 9: around 200.

* Please insert two new pairs of cases where every character appears an even number of times (e.g. some characters appear twice, some 4 times, some 10 times…) and the string isn't periodic (i.e. it isn't a repetition of a shorter substring). The length of the input should be around 50.

  • In one pair, the string cannot become empty (i.e. output is -1).

  • In the other pair, the string can become empty (i.e. output is not -1), and the aim is to provide players with a smaller case where different removal orders produce different total costs for easier debugging.

Thanks.

Thank you for following up on my earlier comment. Regarding the updated contribution:

Cases
* Please split Test 2 and Validator 2 into two pairs:

  (a) The current Test 2 and a new validator should cover the scenario where every character appears an even number of times. (Test 2 should remain unchanged.)

  (b) A new test and the current Validator 2 should cover the scenario where some characters appear an even number of times while others appear an odd number of times. (Validator 2 should remain unchanged.)

* Please insert a new pair of cases satisfying all of the following conditions:

  • Every character appears an even number of times (e.g. some characters appear twice, some 4 times, some 10 times…).
  
  • The string isn't periodic (i.e. it isn't a repetition of a shorter substring).

  • The length of the string should be around 50.

  • The string cannot become empty (i.e. the output is -1).

Thanks again.
Please follow up the comment above to improve the test coverage. Thanks.
